source_text: V. Τούτων δὲ καὶ ἄλλων πολλῶν λεχθέντων, ὡς ἐπὶ πολὺ μὴ σιωπῆσαι τὸν Πιόνιον, ὅ τε νεωκόρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπέστησαν τὰς ἀκοάς, ὥστε τοσαύτην ἡσυχίαν γενέσθαι ὡς μηδὲ γρῦξαί τινα. Εἰπόντος δὲ πάλιν τοῦ Πιονίου ὅτι Τοῖς θεοῖς ὑμῶν οὐ λατρεύομεν καὶ τῇ εἰκόνι τῇ χρυσῇ οὐ προσκυνοῦμεν, ἤγαγον αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὕπαιθρον εἰς τὸ μέσον, καὶ περιέστησαν αὐτοῖς τινες τῶν ἀγοραίων ἅμα τῷ Πολέμωνι ἐκλιπαροῦντες καὶ λέγοντες· Πείσθητι ἡμῖν, Πιόνιε, ὅτι σε φιλοῦμεν, καὶ διὰ πολλὰ ἄξιος εἶ ζῆν, ἤθους τε ἕνεκα καὶ ἐπιεικείας. Καλόν ἐστι τὸ ζῆν καὶ τὸ φῶς τοῦτο βλέπειν· καὶ ἄλλα τινὰ πλείονα. Ὁ δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς κἀγὼ λέγω ὅτι καλὸν ἔστι τὸ ζῆν, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνο κρεῖσσον ὃ ἡμεῖς ἐπιποθοῦμεν. Καὶ τὸ φῶς, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκεῖνο τὸ ἀληθινόν. Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν οὖν ἅπαντα καλά· καὶ οὐχ ὡς θανατιῶντες ἢ μισοῦντες τὰ ἔργα τοῦ θεοῦ φεύγομεν, ἀλλ᾽ ἑτέρων μεγάλων ὑπερβολῇ τούτων καταφρονοῦμεν ἐνεδρευόντων ἡμᾶς.
pass_a_gloss: When these things and many other things had been said, since for the most part Pionius did not keep silent, both the temple-warden and those with him and all the crowd directed their ears, so that so great a stillness came to be that no one even muttered. When Pionius again said that we do not serve your gods and we do not bow to the golden image, they led them into the open courtyard into the middle, and some of the marketplace men with Polemon stood around them earnestly entreating and saying: Be persuaded by us, Pionius, because we love you, and for many reasons you are worthy to live, both for character and for gentleness. It is good to live and to see this light, and many other things besides. He said to them: I also say that to live is good, but that which we long for is better. And the light is good, but I mean the true one. These things therefore are all good; and not as condemning or hating the works of God do we flee, but by the surpassing greatness of other great things we despise these present things that lie in ambush for us.
pass_b_english: When these words and many others had been spoken, and Pionius had for the most part refused to fall silent, the temple-warden and his companions and the whole crowd turned their ears to listen, so that a stillness fell so deep that no one uttered even a murmur. Yet when Pionius said again, We do not serve your gods, nor do we bow down to the golden image, they led them out into the open court and placed them in the middle.

Then some men from the marketplace came and stood around them together with Polemon, pleading with him and saying, Be persuaded by us, Pionius, for we love you, and on many counts you deserve to live, for your character and your gentleness. It is good to be alive and to behold this light, with many more words besides. He answered them, I too say that life is good, but the life we long for is better. The light is good, but I mean the true light. All these present things are indeed good. We do not turn away because we condemn or hate the works of God, but because far greater things surpass them, we hold these present things in contempt, though they lie in ambush to trap us.
